title: Log-Normal Multiplicative Dynamics for Stable Low-Precision Deep Learning
claim: Our method trains large models from scratch at low precision without degradation, while baseline optimizers fail or become unstable.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared legend style, ours in red/blue, baselines gray
description: Two side-by-side line plots of training curves, with a legend inside each panel. The left panel, titled 'Vision Transformer on ImageNet', plots top-1 test accuracy (30–80) against epoch (0–200). The right panel, titled 'GPT-2 (124M) on OpenWebText', plots validation perplexity (18–32) against step (0–25, ×10³). Each panel has five curves. AdamW, AdamW with MXFP6 forward pass, and Madam are drawn in gray with different markers: circle, asterisk and diamond. LMD is red with circles and LMD with MXFP6 forward pass is blue with asterisks. The two LMD curves overlap almost exactly and end highest on ViT and lowest on GPT-2. The gray baselines plateau lower on ViT. On GPT-2, Madam stays far above the rest and AdamW with MXFP6 plateaus higher. The eye goes first to the bright red and blue curves against the gray ones.
caption: These two plots demonstrate that LMD enables full-scratch learning of Vision Transformer and GPT-2. Even when the forward pass is performed using low-precision formats based on the Microscaling data format (MXFP6), no performance degradation occurs. AdamW and Madam are unable to sufficiently train ViT. On GPT-2, AdamW shows perplexity similar to LMD, but we can observe that the optimizer can not stably learn using low-precision forward-passes. For GPT-2 training, LMD and Madam use a sequence length of 4096 and a batch size of 16. Note that AdamW uses a sequence length of 1024 and a batch size of 64. However, the number of tokens per step is the same. All training, except for the forward passes in MXFP6, was performed using bfloat16.
abstract: We propose Log-Normal Multiplicative Dynamics (LMD), a new algorithm to stabilize low-precision deep learning. LMD is motivated by the robustness of biological neural networks where synaptic spine sizes follow a log-normal distribution and fluctuate via noisy multiplicative dynamics. So far, no algorithm has successfully incorporated all these synaptic properties to train large models. LMD incorporates these properties through a variational Bayesian formulation that uses a log-normal posterior over weights. We evaluate LMD with low-precision forward-pass matrix multiplications, including training a Vision Transformer and GPT-2 from scratch. Our findings demonstrate the utility of biologically inspired approaches for designing energy-efficient algorithms for stable low-precision deep learning.
